title: Staggered cut tiers & canary windows plan for API/Console/Runtime release train
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: define and document a staggered scope-lock and cut criteria approach for the next unified release train covering API, Console, and Runtime. This ticket proposes three cut tiers (Tier 1: Blocker & Security; Tier 2: High-impact UX/Runtime changes; Tier 3: Backlog+non-blocking improvements), phased scope-lock dates, and a canary rollout window plan to reduce regression risk and coordinate release notes across teams.

Summary of the proposal:
- Cut tiers: clearly classify PRs/features into Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3 during triage. Only Tier 1 allowed after Tier 1 lock; Tier 2 allowed until Tier 2 lock; Tier 3 frozen at Tier 3 lock. Tier definitions include acceptance criteria and rollback requirements.
- Staggered locks: three incremental scope-lock dates spaced 7 days apart to give teams rolling finalization windows while preventing last-minute high-risk changes.
- Canary windows: define two canary waves for hosted API and Dedicated: 48h internal canary (alpha customers + internal traffic), followed by 72h broader canary (beta customers + limited region). Console and Runtime have synchronized canaries tied to canary policies for autoscale and kernel selection changes.
- Release notes coordination: central owner and per-team contributors. Use templated CHANGELOG entries and a shared spreadsheet for final sign-off.
- Rollback and fallback: explicit rollback playbooks per tier, automatic routing fallback to previous model variant for runtime regressions, and observable SLO checks to trigger rollback.

Why this is different: many previous runbooks describe a single scope-freeze. This plan intentionally trades slower freeze for safer, tiered gating, enabling targeted exceptions while preserving predictable launch windows for cross-team marketing and partner comms.
acceptance_criteria: Tier definitions documented and published in Confluence
Scope-lock calendar with three lock dates posted and accepted by ENG/DES/OPS
Canary windows scheduled and on-call rotations assigned
Release notes template and owner for each subsystem assigned
Rollback playbooks drafted for Tier 1 and Tier 2 with thresholds mapped to SLOs
gating_checklist: Performance benchmarks for Runtime changes (latency p95 under target)
E2E flows in Console validated against sample orgs
Docs & SDK owners assigned for changelog entries
communication_plan: Day -3: publish draft release notes and updates to partner channel
Canary Day 0: internal comms with on-call and customer success
Canary Day 2/4: public beta announcement to selected customers
GA: general announcement + aggregated release notes and migration guidance
